natural-resource.def: Something from nature that people use, such as water, soil, fish, forests, oil or sunlight. Renewable resources replace themselves; nonrenewable resources are used up.

sustainability.def: Using land and resources so that people now meet their needs without harming the ability of future people to meet theirs.

land-use.def: How people use an area of land, such as for forest, farms, homes, roads or factories.

environmental-determinism.def: An old, rejected idea that the physical environment, especially climate, decides how people live and behave. It was used to justify European rule over other peoples.

possibilism.def: The idea that the physical environment sets limits and offers options, and people choose how to live within them using their culture and technology.
